name: Portals directory — approval frames
description: Contract-freeze UX artifacts for the Portals Directory: a left-menu directory in the FuzeFront shell where a master-admin sees the portals they can manage and OPENS a chosen portal in a NEW browser tab at that portal's own host URL (launchUrl). Management continues on that host under the existing per-host tenant routing — there is deliberately NO in-app portal switcher and no context switch. Each portal carries an identity tier badge: soft (shares the root Authentik) or hard (its own Authentik instance, e.g. Mendys Robotics). Approving the flow approves its visual + interaction model AND its component/contract build inventory before any UI is written. frontend-test-engineer drives Playwright against these via the data-frame / data-* hooks. PortalsDirectory is a shell page in frontend/src — NOT a new npm package. States are contract: loading, empty, error+retry, suspended (no launch), and the fail-closed permission-denied / read-only case (no manage authority => zero launch affordances).

dataSource.s1Extension: adminPortals list rows extended to return identity_mode ('soft' | 'hard') and launchUrl (absolute URL of the portal's own host — its primary custom domain, or the root host /p/{slug} path route when it has no custom domain). The client renders these directly: identity_mode -> tier badge, launchUrl -> the 'Open portal' anchor href. The client never composes a host from client-held data.
dataSource.scoping: Rows are Permit-ReBAC-scoped to portals the caller may manage. A caller with no manage authority receives the permission-denied / read-only projection (no launch affordances). tenant/actor is resolved from the session, never accepted from the client.

build.packagesNote: No new npm package. PortalsDirectory is a shell page under frontend/src, mounted at /portals in the FuzeFront host shell. Data is fetched via the existing @fuzefront/portal-client (adminPortals list).
dsPrimitivesNeeded: StatusPill — semantic lifecycle pill (active/degraded/suspended); reused, not in @fuzefront/design-system today
DataList / DataTable — the scannable directory list
ExternalLink — new-tab anchor carrying the ↗ affordance and rel="noopener noreferrer"

frames.label: (a) Portals
frames.summary: The master-admin's directory of manageable portals. Each row shows name, primary domain, lifecycle status pill, and a soft/hard identity-tier badge, with a searchable/scannable list and an 'Open portal ↗' action that opens the portal's own host URL in a NEW browser tab.
frames.acceptanceNotes: Rows render from GET /api/v1/admin/portals (cursor-paginated; 'Load more' advances the cursor). The S1 extension supplies identity_mode -> the tier badge (soft = shares root Authentik; hard = own Authentik instance) and launchUrl -> the launch anchor href. 'Open portal' is a plain <a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href={launchUrl}> to the portal's OWN host — never an in-app route, never window.open, never a same-tab navigation that unmounts the shell. launchUrl is server-authoritative (primary custom domain, or root host /p/{slug} path route when none); the client never composes a host. A suspended portal renders no enabled launch affordance. The list is Permit-ReBAC-scoped to portals the caller may manage. Flag fuzefront.platform.portals-directory (default OFF).

frames.label: (b) States
frames.summary: States are contract: loading skeleton, fresh empty (no portals managed yet), list error with retry, the explicit new-tab launch affordance, a suspended row with no launch, and the fail-closed permission-denied / read-only case where a caller without manage authority sees zero launch affordances.
frames.acceptanceNotes: d1 aria-busy skeleton while GET /api/v1/admin/portals is in flight. d2 empty is a REAL non-error case (a caller can legitimately manage zero portals). d3 renders [data-action='retry'] and never a sign-in redirect — the session is intact. d4 the launch action is unmistakably external (new tab + hint). d5 a suspended portal exposes no enabled launch affordance. d6 is the fail-closed contract: a caller without manage authority gets a 403 (data-http='403', data-error-code='FORBIDDEN') shown IN PLACE, and NO launch anchor or button is emitted for any row — the launch column is absent, not merely disabled. Only a 401 re-authenticates.
